title: Whisperwood's Wonderful Voices
markdown:
Deep in Whisperwood, Rafe the fox opened a Public Speaking School. “Every creature,” he announced, “deserves to be heard.”

His students were Pip the squirrel, who chattered fast; Brychan the badger, whose words rumbled; and Cora the duck, who went slap-slap-slap.

Rafe taught them to stand tall. “Confidence,” he boomed, “is the sparkle in your words.”

But learning got silly. Pip puffed out his chest to roar, but only a tiny squeak came out. Brychan wobbled, trying to quack with his whole body. Cora flapped her wings, nearly sending berries rolling.

The next day, Pip whispered so softly you had to sniff him to hear. Brychan jigged while talking about roots, his paws tapping a tap-tap-tap. Cora took a deep breath and rumbled, “The sky is blue,” in a roar that made a ladybug fall off a leaf. Pip’s whisper, Brychan’s jig, Cora’s roar: three voices borrowed, none of them quite home.

Aunt Vi, Cora’s wise aunt, perched nearby. “They are trying,” she told Rafe, her voice soft as moss. “But are they being themselves? It’s like wearing boots too big for your feet.”

Rafe thought. Pip was whispering loudly. Brychan was hopping. Cora was rumbling roars. Aunt Vi was right. They were wearing someone else’s confidence, not their own.

Rafe gathered his students. “Forget roaring and wobbling,” he said gently. “Let the best you shine.”

He told Pip, “Your chatter is like a sparkling stream.” To Brychan, “Your quiet thoughts are like strong oak roots.” And to Cora, “Your happy quacks are like a bright sunny day.”

They tried again. Pip chattered with squirrelly excitement. Brychan shared his thoughts calmly. Cora quacked her joy, wiggling happily. Rafe’s tail swished.

The forest seemed to sigh with relief. Each creature spoke in a voice that fitted, the way a well-worn path fits a familiar paw. Aunt Vi tucked her head under a wing, listening, and the ladybug climbed back onto its leaf.
characters: Rafe (a public-speaking fox), Cora (a slap-slap duck), Aunt Vi (a moss-voiced aunt)
